content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against the facts: the account pages failing for some shoppers, the peak failure rate, the setting that moved those pages onto newer code, and the likely breakage that follows. Each one is supported by the figures and the stated cause.

I'm working through the remaining claims: the shop losing an estimated sum in takings, the lack of any page or linked incident, and the sequence of reverts, where the first one didn't help and the second one did and stayed in place. I'm also checking that the proposed fix is opened as a draft by Argus, which the record supports.

supported.quote: For {duration}, account pages on io-shop failed to load for some shoppers.
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load

supported.quote: At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing.
rows: Requests failing at the worst minute: 35.5% {peak_error_rate}

supported.quote: Turning off a setting moved the account pages onto newer code.
That code likely breaks for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, because it tries to work out an average over zero purchases.
Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 7,533.46 USD {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: Argus first reverted the monthly-spend-feature flag, but that did not help, so Argus put it back.
Argus then reverted the legacy-checkout-fallback flag. That change was confirmed to help and is still in place.
Argus has also opened a proposed fix to the code as a draft.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #560 - opened as a draft
